Reserved Mac Location and signed-package acceptance — @TRIAL@

Generation runs no native tools or app. All cases remain not_run. Automated
Location model tests use controlled native input and the real sixty-second
production timer; profile tests cover invalid bundle IDs, certificate mismatch,
expiry and restricted entitlement spelling. These human steps add actual TCC,
AMFI/Gatekeeper and extension approval/loading observations, not screenshots as
substitutes for behavior. Keep review images/video outside Git.

1. Qualification and ownership.
   Reserve the WHOLE Mac serial @SERIAL@ and fresh ordinary account @ACCOUNT@
   UID @UID@ at the exact inventoried hardware UUID/OS build. System extensions
   are machine-wide: a fresh account on a shared machine is insufficient.
   Confirm the independently recorded empty-machine baseline: no installed
   Wendy Agent, matching system extension, Wendy VPN configuration, active Wendy
   launch job, existing Wendy TCC entry or another user's Wendy process. Require
   owner authorization and a tested whole-machine recovery/restore method before
   proceeding. Do not reset TCC, modify its database, disable SIP/Gatekeeper,
   enable system-extension developer mode, install a trust root or alter an
   unrelated VPN/extension. If a baseline is not empty, use another reserved Mac.
   Record native `sw_vers -buildVersion`, `id -u`, `ioreg` serial/UUID, and
   systemextensionsctl/scutil output. Compare every value with the inventory.
   Capture public evidence only: no private key, profile token or keychain dump.

2. Exact signed artifact checks before installation.
   Compare the ZIP, complete bundle inventory, app executable SHA256 @CANDIDATE@,
   extension executable and both embedded provisioning profiles with the plan.
   Run release-validation against the exact expected certificate SHA1 @SIGNER@;
   it validates profile identity/expiry/certificate and actual signed entitlements,
   then tests the live host/extension signatures against the pinned signer.
   Expected TeamIdentifier is @TEAM@; bundle IDs are sh.wendy.WendyAgentMac and
   sh.wendy.WendyAgentMac.NetProxy. Run gatekeeper and staple and require success
   plus the expected Developer ID/notarization records. Do not resign a rejected
   bundle or remove quarantine to make it pass. The profile plist records used
   at generation are provenance inputs; actual bundled validation is mandatory.
   Inspect the real nonempty NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription in Info.plist.
   The short-lived historical core-only fallback is superseded by the current
   provisioned release; absence of required profiles/extension fails this plan.

   The owner installs ONLY this reviewed bundle into the previously absent
   /Applications/WendyAgentMac.app using the normal signed-app installation
   method. Re-inventory/hash the installed package and rerun its signature check
   before open-installed. Record the new PID, birth time, executable path and
   code signature. Require the process remains alive for at least 30 seconds and
   serves the generated local-info request through the isolated CLI profile; a successful `open`/spctl alone is
   not AMFI launch proof. Never use the repository SmokeTestMacReleaseLaunch.sh
   on a shared account: its bundle-ID quit behavior is broader than this plan.

3. 2243/2004 real unanswered Location request.
   Open the actual menu item 'Welcome & Permissions…' in the pinned app. Leave
   launch-at-login unchanged; no camera/microphone/Bluetooth request is required
   for this case. Confirm the OS-level Location decision is initially pending
   in this fresh account and record global Location Services enabled state.
   Start a monotonic observation before pressing the Location request button.
   Verify the system dialog names the pinned app. Leave it unanswered for at
   least 65 seconds. Request submission and an unchanged status must not report
   Allowed. While pending, repeated clicks must not launch overlapping requests.
   By 75 seconds the spinner must stop and the app must explain exactly that
   macOS has not returned a Location decision and offer retry/System Settings.
   Require the app remains responsive and same PID; restarting is not recovery.
   Save the app's bounded events output around the request/timeout and the
   owner-observed timestamps. If no dialog appears, distinguish a genuinely
   unanswered native request from disabled global services or a missing usage
   description. Those guards must explain their own cause without spinning;
   they cannot satisfy the dialog case. Do not dismiss or grant another app's
   permission prompt. End the pending OS dialog by the owner choosing denial.

4. Denial and recovery on the same installed app.
   Require the actual deny decision to stop waiting promptly and show Denied,
   with no false Allowed result or stale unanswered explanation. Close/reopen
   the permissions view and require the native decision persists. In System
   Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services, the owner may enable only
   this pinned Wendy app for this reserved account. Bring the app back to the
   foreground: require status refreshes to Allowed without app restart, extra
   request or unrelated permission changes. Record PID/birth throughout and a
   fresh generated local-info response. Revoke only this app's Location access and
   require Denied again; then restore the recorded owner-approved baseline for
   this trial. TCC deletion/reset is not a cleanup command. For a separately
   unanswered retry→Allow scenario, use a second fresh reserved account/trial;
   do not claim a denied status can open a brand-new native prompt without the
   OS allowing it. Unanswered, Denied and Allowed each require actual evidence.

5. 2189 shipped release applicability.
   Current AppDelegate hardcodes meshVPNIsEnabled=false. On the unmodified
   candidate, require no Wendy Mesh activation entry, no automatic extension
   activation/approval request and no unexpected Wendy VPN becoming enabled.
   Capture extension/VPN state before and after launch. This is current shipped
   behavior. Signature validity and launch success DO NOT prove extension
   loading; do not invent an activation CLI command or an unavailable menu.

6. Optional separately signed extension-validation build.
   The generated validation-AppDelegate.swift changes only the reviewed private
   gate to true. It is an instrumentation source, not an installed binary and
   not a shipped-release result. On an isolated source checkout at the pinned
   revision, the authorized release owner applies that exact overlay and builds
   using the unchanged production Build.sh, actual Developer ID/profile inputs
   and normal notarization. Preserve source diff/hash, build logs, signer,
   profiles, immutable ZIP and full bundle inventory in validation_build record.
   Use new host and extension bundle versions so OS replacement cannot silently
   use a cached extension. Re-run generation with validation_bundle/validation_zip
   and the build record; no validation artifact means this case stays pending.

   Quit the owned candidate normally and confirm its PID/listener has ended.
   Only the owner replaces the candidate at the exact reserved /Applications
   path with this separately validated/notarized build. Run validation-release-
   check, validation-gatekeeper and validation-staple against its input bundle,
   then rehash/validate the installed copy before launching. Record its distinct
   executable hash/PID. Never mutate or ad-hoc sign the already reviewed bundle.

   The real MeshVPNController first reads this reserved account's ~/.wendy/
   config.json and refreshes its Cloud directory before installation. Use only
   the separately owner-approved reserved Cloud profile/tenant and exact test
   peer in the hashed records; the app does NOT read the CLI WENDY_CONFIG_DIR
   override here. Do not copy another user's identity or output secrets. If the
   profile/directory is unavailable, fail at that prerequisite, not at extension
   loading. In the validation build's actual 'Wendy Mesh' menu, request connect.
   Observe activation/approval state and the exact app/team/bundle identifier.
   Initially leave system-extension approval unanswered for 30 seconds: the app
   must report needs approval rather than claim an active VPN. Then approve only
   the owned @TEAM@ / sh.wendy.WendyAgentMac.NetProxy request using the OS prompt
   or indicated Network Extension Settings. No security bypass is allowed.

   Within 120 seconds require systemextensionsctl reports that exact bundle/team
   enabled and activated at the validation version, actual provider start logs,
   and scutil/network-extension state for both configured app-proxy and packet
   providers. 'Activated' alone does not show provider startup. Require fresh
   exact TCP request/response bytes to the independently provisioned test peer
   through the mesh address, with peer-side nonce/time receipt and no ordinary
   LAN/Cloud bypass, using the qualified topology/traffic commands in
   extension_peer record. That record must specify its actual immutable test
   service, endpoint, challenge bytes and expected digest; without it data-path
   acceptance remains pending. Observe failure/refusal distinctly from approval.
   Disconnect using the validation app menu, require its VPN sessions stop, then
   reconnect once without another approval and require new traffic. Preserve
   installer/provider logs and before/after extension/VPN state. This proves
   the instrumented real installer/providers, never the shipped disabled entry.

7. Original-failure controls and cleanup.
   Existing provisioning tests reject wrong bundle ID, expired profile, wrong
   certificate and legacy entitlement values; do not install deliberately bad
   signed artifacts as a shortcut. Automated Location controls restore early
   completion and the unbounded wait and must fail at their precise assertions.
   If doing a physical historical control, the release owner must supply a
   separately reviewed/signed compatible package and recovery record; no guessed
   downgrade or TCC reset is generated. Unsupported historical controls remain
   pending, not evidence against the current package.

   Disconnect the owned validation app, quit it and prove PID/provider sessions
   are gone. Use only the owner's supported exact-app System Settings/Finder
   removal sequence recorded before the trial. A reboot may be required for the
   OS to finish removal; verify systemextensionsctl and scutil against the empty
   baseline afterward. Never use systemextensionsctl reset/uninstall with disabled
   SIP, erase global NetworkExtension preferences or delete unrelated jobs. If
   the OS cannot remove the exact extension normally, retain the machine as an
   incomplete trial and use its preapproved whole-machine restore; account
   deletion alone does not remove machine-wide extension state. Restore only
   the reserved account/device according to its owner record. Physical cases
   become accepted only after their observations and cleanup are complete.

Apple platform prerequisites (primary references, reviewed during preparation):
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions/installing-system-extensions-and-drivers
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions/ossystemextensionrequest
